A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same YRC-0/YRC-Bench work despite the changed title and publication format. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and matchable.

before.justification: v2 reports original coordination-policy experiments across 19 environments, including performance comparisons, oracle-component analyses and feature comparisons in Section 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 6 and Appendix D. Their retention from v2 does not change their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The coordination wrapper, weakened-novice validator, percentile-based threshold selection, Deep SVDD implementation and RLOracle procedure remain the same. Added explanations do not establish an algorithm or architecture change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three MiniGrid environments, eleven Procgen games and five CLIPort tasks described in Appendix C. No additional domain, task or distribution-shift scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: The five logit-based methods, Deep SVDD variants, four rule-based baselines and RLOracle remain in the corresponding comparisons. Deep Ensembles and MC Dropout are newly discussed as alternatives, but neither is evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 retains half-length PPO training for weakened MiniGrid/Procgen novices and 10 versus 100 demonstrations for CLIPort. However, new Appendix D.8.2 describes weakening generally as using 50% of the data/epochs. It is unclear whether this is an overgeneralized summary or a reported CLIPort budget revision. Other evaluation settings match.

E4.justification: Existing oracle-component comparisons, feature analyses and success cases are retained. New Appendices D.7–D.8 interpret existing figures and discuss hypothetical weakening choices; they report no new plunder experiment, sensitivity test or validator-ranking analysis.

E5.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same bootstrap procedure and parameters, including 1,000 simulations, 1,600 episodes and samples of 256. Standard-deviation reporting is unchanged. New discussion of overlapping error bars, possible seed effects and potential ranking correlations introduces no new statistical estimates.

E6.justification: The result graphics and numerical entries are retained. Both versions report a maximum of three environment wins per method, validated methods winning collectively in 14 of 19 environments, and substantial oracle-proposer improvements in 10 of 19. New appendix prose discusses already displayed results.

T1.justification: Section 3 softens the stated high-training/low-test novice-performance assumption by explicitly describing it as a typical consequence of distribution shift rather than a hard requirement. The MDP, reward and metric equations remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: v3 foregrounds the existing proposer-validator decomposition as a diagnostic contribution in the abstract and scopes it to threshold/selection methods in Section 3, replacing v2's broader statement about what solving YRC-0 requires. The benchmark, validation strategy and headline experimental claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands interpretation: it attributes uncertainty-method failures to systematic biases, qualifies the proposer-bottleneck inference because error bars overlap, hypothesizes why the oracle proposer underperforms in plunder, and explains the weakening choice. It also expands deployment restrictions and baseline-selection rationale. These are substantive explanatory changes without additional experimental support.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly documents using the full training distribution instead of a held-out validation subset and freezing novice/coordination parameters during deployment. Existing implementation descriptions, code access, hardware and runtime information remain. The new generalized weakening-budget description introduces the ambiguity noted under E3.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds connections to online imitation learning, safe RL, uncertainty quantification and meta-learning, citing Cohen et al. (2022), Xue-Song et al. (2023), Lockwood and Si (2022), and Hospedales et al. (2021). These extend the retained research positioning; conversion to author-year citations is stylistic.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially revised around competence assessment under distribution shift, with expanded motivation, problem explanation, baseline rationale and rewritten results discussion. The title and Section 5 heading change, five findings become four, and explanatory Appendices D.7–D.8 are added.

P2.justification: The document receives a comprehensive TMLR reformatting, changing typography, margins, author layout, running headers and figure/table placement. The same twelve figures and two tables remain; for example, Figure 12 and Table 2 now share page 24 instead of occupying separate pages in v2.

improvement.justification: v3 usefully scopes the diagnostic framework and makes the proposer-bottleneck interpretation more cautious. However, its stronger causal assertions about uncertainty-method failures lack corresponding analyses, and Appendix D.8 does not reconcile its general 50% weakening description with the retained CLIPort 10/100 setting. With the empirical evidence unchanged, clearer framing and qualifications coexist with new problems in precision and evidential support, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
